question: Describe thermionic emission, field emission and photoelectric emission. Explain how these processes differ on the basis of the type of energy supplied to electrons.

options.A: Thermionic emission is due to light, field emission is due to heat, and photoelectric emission is due to a magnetic field.
options.B: All three emissions occur without any energy being supplied to electrons.
options.C: Thermionic emission and photoelectric emission are identical, while field emission is due to photon collisions.
options.D: Thermionic emission uses heat energy, field emission uses a strong electric field, and photoelectric emission uses light of suitable frequency. In each case electrons must overcome the metal work function.
